name: OCAT Shenzhen
funding: Founded 2005 and owned by OCT Group, a central state-owned tourism and property group. OCT cut funding sharply in 2023 to venue costs only; OCAT must earn its own income.
watch: Beijing, Shanghai and Xi'an venues were suspended in 2022 and their work moved here. OCAT Shanghai closed in 2021 after a video outcry.
records_note: The official site blocks automated access with a Cloudflare check, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; searches found none of them.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá
watch: Fundación BAT (British American Tobacco Colombia) is a 2025 gala private donor; March 2026 row over curator Eugenio Viola's dismissal, nepotism and labour claims (170 signatories).
why_flagged: Fundación BAT (British American Tobacco Colombia) is a 2025 gala private donor; March 2026 row over curator Eugenio Viola's dismissal, nepotism and labour claims (170 signatories).
records_note: MAMBO publishes no annual report, accounts or board; its gala page shows sponsor logos grouped by year, 2023 to 2025.

name: Museo La Tertulia
funding: Private museum, ~2,000 works (2025); funded by Colegio Alemán de Cali as major patron, Bancolombia, Fundación Sura, Comfandi and Fundación Scarpetta Gnecco.
watch: Supporter roster unverified. Roster is the museum's own June 2025 statement; museolatertulia.com is now a link page. Bancolombia (bank) and Sura (insurer) named.
records_note: Its web address redirects to a Linktree page of ticket links and a friends-program file; no reports, accounts, funder list or board are published.

name: Museo de Antioquia
funding: Ministerio de las Culturas, Alcaldía de Medellín, Área Metropolitana; aliados include EPM, Bancolombia, SURA, Mineros, Metro de Medellín, Comfama and the Chamber of Commerce.
records_note: Shows a page of allies as undated logos with alt text, and publishes no annual reports, accounts or board list.

name: Ordrupgaard
funding: State museum since 1953 on insurer Wilhelm Hansen's bequest; Finn Juhl House funded by a private donor.
watch: Augustinus Fonden and Det Obelske Familiefond both hold Scandinavian Tobacco Group stakes. ordrupgaard.dk is currently a suspended-account page.
why_flagged: Augustinus Fonden and Det Obelske Familiefond both hold Scandinavian Tobacco Group stakes. ordrupgaard.dk is currently a suspended-account page.
records_note: Ordrupgaard, a state museum, posts its 2024 and 2025 annual reports with full accounts, but names no funders and lists no board.

name: Copenhagen Contemporary
funding: Culture Ministry, City of Copenhagen, Statens Kunstfond and 15 foundations in 2026, including Augustinusfonden, Det Obelske Familiefond, A.P. Møller, Ny Carlsberg, Nordea and Spar Nord.
watch: Augustinus Fonden's investment company holds over 25% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group; Det Obelske Familiefond's C.W. Obel A/S holds over 10% (May 2025).
records_note: It posts annual reports with accounts for 2022 to 2024, names its five board members and lists 22 supporters for 2026.

name: HEART Herning
funding: Collection founded by shirt manufacturer Aage Damgaard; current roster not found.
watch: The 2023 report, the latest posted, also names A.P. Møller, Ny Carlsberg, Ole Kirk's Fond (LEGO family), Beckett-Fonden and Statens Kunstfond.
why_flagged: The 2023 report, the latest posted, also names A.P. Møller, Ny Carlsberg, Ole Kirk's Fond (LEGO family), Beckett-Fonden and Statens Kunstfond.
records_note: HEART posts annual reports from 2009 to 2023 with audited accounts, lists six board members, and names its foundation funders in the 2022 report.

name: Contemporary Image Collective
funding: No funder list is published. The Arab Fund for Arts and Culture lists a 2024 CiC project under Egypt's National Cultural Opportunities Fund. Cairo artists depend on foreign grants.
records_note: Its website fails certificate checks and could not be opened. A 2022 archived homepage shows only labs, a library and contact details.

name: Museum of Modern Egyptian Art
watch: Holds more than 13,000 works. Ahram Online reported a partial closure; no removed or censored works are documented.
records_note: No official site was found; searches returned only third-party pages, so no reports, accounts, funder list or board are published that we could find.

name: Zoma Museum
funding: Founders Elias Sime and Meskerem Assegued bought the Mekanisa land from 2013 with their own money and sales of Sime's art. Dire Dawa city gave the Harla land in 2007.
records_note: Its website now serves gambling spam, so nothing about its reports, accounts, funders or board could be checked.

name: Kunsthalle Tbilisi
funding: Roving space founded 2018 by Irena Popiashvili and Lika Chkuaseli; mostly private donors with a small municipal share (unnamed).
watch: UNVERIFIED: Donors not named. Site unreachable; Wayback copies of home and about pages (2023, 2025) name no donors.
records_note: Its archived site has one About paragraph naming two founders; no reports, accounts, supporters or board appear.

name: Nubuke Foundation
funding: Private foundation from 2006. Funded through the EU and OACPS ACP-EU Culture programme (AWA consortium with Institut français) and the British Council Digital Collaboration Fund.
watch: Runs the Centre for Clay and Textiles in Wa. The funders page gives no years. No oil, mining or other flagged funder found.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the Funders page names the EU, British Council and Google Arts and Culture, undated, and six board members are listed.
